subject: Polity
description: Covers Money Bills and Vote on Account.

questions.stem: In the context of the Indian Parliament, what is a 'Money Bill'?

options.option_text: A bill that exclusively deals with taxation, borrowing of money, or expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India
Any bill introduced by the Finance Minister
A bill related to the salaries of Members of Parliament
A bill that regulates foreign direct investment in Indian banks

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: According to Article 110 of the Constitution, a bill is deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains ONLY provisions dealing with the imposition/abolition of taxes, government borrowing, or the custody/appropriation of money out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
DECOY BUSTING: A bill dealing with fines or fees for licenses is explicitly NOT a Money Bill. A Financial Bill may contain taxation clauses but also other non-financial matters.
EXAM INSIGHT: A Money Bill can ONLY be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and only on the prior recommendation of the President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Who has the absolute final authority to decide whether a particular bill is a 'Money Bill' or not?

options.option_text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Article 110(3) explicitly states that if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha thereon shall be final. When a Money Bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, the Speaker heavily endorses it as a Money Bill.
DECOY BUSTING: The President recommends its introduction, but the Speaker classifies it. The Supreme Court cannot generally question the Speaker's classification due to parliamentary privilege.
EXAM INSIGHT: This power is highly significant because if a bill is certified as a Money Bill, the Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend it; they can only delay it for a maximum of 14 days.

questions.stem: What is a 'Vote on Account' in the Indian Parliamentary system?

options.option_text: A special provision allowing the government to withdraw funds for a few months before the full budget is passed
A vote taken to estimate the black money in the economy
A procedure to audit the accounts of the ruling political party
A vote to pass the final budget at the end of the financial year

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The presentation and passing of the full Union Budget takes several months (usually stretching past the April 1st start of the new financial year). To keep the government running and pay salaries during this interim period, the Lok Sabha grants an advance grant called a 'Vote on Account' (usually equal to 1/6th of the total estimated expenditure) under Article 116.
DECOY BUSTING: It has nothing to do with auditing, black money, or the final passing of the budget. It is strictly an advance cash withdrawal mechanism.
EXAM INSIGHT: In election years, the outgoing government presents an 'Interim Budget' instead of a full budget, which heavily relies on a Vote on Account until the new government is formed.
